slice: Round 2 slice A+B: known issues, recalls, supersessions (all makes 2020-2026) and supercross/arenacross setups

records.statement: In May 2025 about 19,310 US and 3,870 Canadian GasGas and Husqvarna bikes from 2022-2025 were recalled because the front brake caliper can crack and lose braking; stop riding and have a dealer inspect and, if needed, repair it free.

source.name: US Consumer Product Safety Commission recall notice (KTM AG / KTM North America)

records.notes: Regulator notice. Covers GasGas MC/EX/EC 2023-2025 (EC 250/300 from 2022; MC 150, MC 300 and EW 500F also listed but not in the BAK roster) and Husqvarna 2022 TE 150i/250i/300i, FE 350/501; 2023 FE 450, FX 350, FX 450, TE 150/250/300, TX 300; 2024 FE 450, TE 150/250/300. This is the Braktec front-caliper recall an existing record mentions only for MC 250F; KTM-branded bikes (Brembo) are not included. Husqvarna MX models (FC/TC) are not listed. Owner line 888-985-6090.

records.statement: Australia recalled 2022-2025 GasGas MC and EX bikes with Braktec brakes because the front caliper may crack and break, causing brake failure; stop riding and have a GasGas dealer inspect it free.

source.name: Australian Competition and Consumer Commission Product Safety Australia recall (KTM Australia)

records.notes: Australian list also includes MC 150 and MC 300 (not in the BAK roster). Unit count not stated on the page (VIN list attached).

records.topic: EC front brake caliper recall (Australia, REC-006266)
records.statement: In Australia 1,776 GasGas EC enduro bikes (EC 250 and EC 300 2022-2025, EC 450F 2024-2025) were recalled because a manufacturing defect can let the front brake caliper crack and break.

source.name: Australian Government Vehicle Recalls (KTM Australia)

records.notes: Page header gives a 2021-2024 model-year range but the variant list says 2022-2025; recorded in conflicts. Also covers EC 125, EC 250F, EC 350F, EC 500F (not in roster).

records.topic: EC front caliper split-pin recall (Australia, REC-004948)
records.statement: About 1,185 Australian GasGas EC bikes from 2021-2022 were recalled because the front caliper split pins that hold the pad bracket may be fitted backwards and fall out, letting the bracket detach; a dealer re-fits them free. Owners can check that the split pins are in place and secured.

source.name: Australian Government Vehicle Recalls (KTM Australia)

records.notes: Listing range says 2020-2021 but the defect text says MY21 and MY22. Also covers EC 250F and EC 350F (not in roster).

records.topic: rear brake caliper recall: full model scope (CPSC fast-track, Aug 2026)
records.statement: The August 2026 rear-caliper recall (about 21,040 US and 4,140 Canadian bikes) is wider than off-road models: it also covers 2021-2024 GasGas MC 125, MC 250, MC 250F, MC 350F and MC 450F plus EC/EX models, and 2022-2024 Husqvarna TE, TX, FE and FX models. The caliper can crack; stop riding until repaired.

values.type: CPSC Fast Track, joint with Transport Canada

source.name: RideApart summary of the CPSC/Transport Canada notice

records.notes: Secondary report of the regulator notice; the existing ktm_offroad_4t record lists only Husqvarna FX/FE and GasGas EX/EC four-strokes. NHTSA documents 26V443 relate to this campaign. No injuries reported at announcement.

records.topic: 2022 125/150 CDI rev-limiter connecting rod recall (US, CPSC 22-762)
records.statement: About 3,310 2022 KTM 125 SX, 125 XC, 150 SX, Husqvarna TC 125 and GasGas MC 125 bikes were recalled in July 2022 because the CDI rev-limiter setting can let the connecting rod break; dealers replace the CDI box free. A 2022 125/150 bought used should be checked for this repair.

source.name: US CPSC recall alert (KTM North America); Transport Canada 2022141

records.notes: Transport Canada notice (https://recalls-rappels.canada.ca/en/alert-recall/transport-canada-recall-2022141) names the CDI rev-limiter as the cause and gives the same five models. No incidents reported in the US notice.

records.statement: In Australia 260 2022 KTM 125 SX and 150 SX bikes were recalled because the rev-limiter setting may let the connecting rod break; the repair is free.

source.name: ACCC Product Safety Australia (KTM Australia)

records.statement: In Australia 86 2022 GasGas MC 125 bikes were recalled because the rev-limiter setting may let the connecting rod break; repair is free.

source.name: ACCC Product Safety Australia (KTM Australia)

records.notes: A matching Husqvarna TC 125 Australian extended recall page exists (HQVA Pty Ltd) but was not fetched.

records.statement: Five 2021 KTM 450 SX-F bikes in Australia were recalled because a defective shift drum may have been fitted and could break while riding; dealers replace it free.

source.name: ACCC Product Safety Australia (KTM Australia)

records.notes: Very small batch; no matching US/Canadian notice was found in this search round.

records.statement: 2021 GasGas MC 125, MC 250F and MC 450F bikes built between 20 November 2020 and 13 January 2021 were recalled in Australia because the drive chain may break or come loose; dealers replace the chain free.

source.name: ACCC Product Safety Australia (KTM Australia)

records.notes: Unit count differs between the ACCC page (201) and a copy of the notice on a consumer forum (197); see conflicts. Same period as Honda's 2021 CRF450R drive-chain recall, suggesting a common chain batch issue is possible but not confirmed.

records.statement: Australia recalled CRF250R/RX/RW and CRF450R/RX/RW bikes built 25 July 2024 to 15 April 2026 because the handlebar may not be clamped tightly enough and can move; stop riding until inspected, with parts due mid-May 2026.

source.name: YourLifeChoices summary of the Honda Australia recall

records.notes: Australian counterpart to US CPSC 26-458 (already in honda450/honda250 files). Unit count not stated; PRA number not given in the article.

records.statement: Australian 2022 KX250 and KX450 bikes sold 1 June 2021 to 22 March 2023 were recalled because a badly made fuel pump can cause hard starting and a stall that will not restart; dealers check and replace the pump.

source.name: ACCC recall advertisement (Kawasaki Motors Pty Ltd)

records.notes: Australian counterpart to the US 2022 KX fuel pump recall already in kawasaki.json. Symptom to watch: hard starting or stalling that will not restart.

records.statement: About 760 2022 YZ125s were recalled in April 2022 because the gear shift assembly can come loose from the crankcase and shift gears on its own; dealers repair it free.

source.name: US CPSC recall alert (Yamaha Motor Corp. USA)

records.notes: Early warning signs: unexpected gear changes or failure to select a gear.

records.statement: Yamaha Australia says the 2022 YZ125 shift selector detent spring may dislodge, causing unexpected shifts or no gear selection; dealers did a free inspection and temporary fix, with repair parts from the end of February 2022.

source.name: ACCC Product Safety Australia (Yamaha Motor Australia)

records.notes: Names the exact failed part (detent spring) that the US notice describes only as the gear shift assembly.

records.topic: hydraulic clutch cuts out: pinched crankcase breather hose
records.statement: If the hydraulic clutch sometimes works and sometimes has no lever pressure, check the crankcase breather hose routing before replacing the slave cylinder: a pinched hose builds crankcase pressure that pushes the slave cylinder back. It is often caused by wrong routing after greasing the linkage.

values.false_fix: new slave cylinder and bleed did not cure it

source.name: Keefer Inc. Testing

records.notes: Found on a 2023 Husqvarna FC 350 test bike; the tester says dealers and owners see the same after linkage service. Applied to the 2023-on four-stroke MX family that shares the hose layout; earlier and off-road models may be similar but are not confirmed.

records.statement: One owner made neutral easier to find by machining the neutral notch of the shift star about 1/32 in (0.8 mm) deeper, a two-hour job; others warn it can cause false neutrals from 2nd and extra wear, so it is not recommended. The usual fix remains selecting neutral as revs drop with the clutch in.

values.labour: about 2 h (clutch and side cover off)

source.name: Vital MX forum thread

records.notes: Single owner's result, disputed by several replies (false-neutral and liability concerns). The owner says KTM changed the detent-lever part material in 2018. Model not named; recorded against the SX-F family as the likely bikes. Not a manufacturer fix.

records.statement: One owner's 2020 250 XC-F seized its cams at about 20 hours after debris blocked an oil passage; he had seen metal on the drain-plug magnet at the first two oil changes. Metal on the magnet or filter early on is a warning sign worth a dealer check.

source.name: Vital MX forum thread

records.notes: Single report; cause disputed (dealer blamed debris introduced at an oil change, owner disagreed). Not evidence of a pattern; recorded for its early-warning value only.

records.statement: Pro supercross bikes run up to about 25% more compression damping than for motocross, with stiffer fork springs, slightly stiffer shock springs and more rebound, and sit lower for stability in the whoops. The aim is not to bottom on big jumps and triples while keeping traction out of turns.

source.name: World Supercross Championship technical feature (suspension specialist interview)

records.notes: Pro-level kit suspension; about 90% of setup is done in pre-season testing and 10% on the day. Rider preference splits on the rear: some want it soft out of flat turns, others stiffer for traction on slick tracks. Amateurs on stock suspension should move in the same direction in smaller steps. Exact publication date not shown; year approximate.

records.statement: Supercross teams usually run a rear sprocket 2-3 teeth larger than for motocross for quicker pull out of short sections, then fine-tune by one rear tooth for dirt and weather while leaving the front sprocket alone (one front tooth equals about three rear).

source.name: Just Bikes feature on an Australian supercross team's YZ450F

records.notes: Source predates 2020 (2010-11 YZ450F) but the principle is model-independent. A rider wanting a calmer bike went the other way: taller gearing and lower revs. For an amateur 450 this direction often means one or two teeth more on the rear; check against BAK speed-per-gear tables.

records.statement: Supercross sections are short, so teams want sharper throttle response, but on hard-packed tracks they richen the low-range fuelling to soften the hit; wet rounds get a separate ignition curve.

values.low_range: richer on hard pack to mellow
values.track_change: usually one curve per SX track; separate wet curve

source.name: Just Bikes feature on an Australian supercross team's YZ450F

records.notes: Older programmable-ignition era; on current bikes the equivalent is the mellow map or traction control on slick or hard-pack dirt. Exhaust was left unchanged.

records.statement: Supercross dirt is usually harder-packed, so teams pick the hard-terrain tyre where an outdoor track would get an intermediate, switch to a soft or sand tyre in mud, and pick after sighting laps; scoop rear tyres show up on rutted or muddy nights.

source.name: Just Bikes team feature (2011); Vital MX Pit Bits 2024 Daytona and 2026 Indianapolis

records.notes: The pit reports (https://www.vitalmx.com/features/vital-mx-pit-bits-2024-daytona-supercross, https://www.vitalmx.com/features/vital-mx-pit-bits-2026-indianapolis-supercross) note scoop tyres on the soft, rutted Daytona and Indianapolis tracks. No published supercross tyre pressures were found.

records.topic: tyre pressure baseline (useful indoors on hard pack)
records.statement: A tester's 2025 pressure baseline runs 12-14 psi: Dunlop MX34 13 front/12.5 rear, MX33 12.5/12, Pirelli MX32 Mid Soft Stadium 13/13.5, MX32 Mid Hard 13.5/13. Riders over 220 lb add 0.5-1 psi, and pressure rises as tyres heat, so recheck after long sessions.

source.name: Keefer Inc. Testing tire pressure settings 2025

records.notes: General motocross baselines with standard or HD tubes, not supercross-specific. Indoors the dirt is slick and hard, so most riders stay at the low end; heat build-up matters less in short arenacross motos.

records.topic: stadium vs supercross vs outdoor: pro teams swap setups
records.statement: When a stadium round is built like an outdoor track, nearly every pro team swaps from its supercross suspension and chassis setup to its outdoor one, several move from air forks to spring forks, and some re-gear and cut new chains for the bigger layout. Supercross setup is a separate, firmer package, not a clicker tweak.

values.change: SX setup -> outdoor setup for open stadium layouts

source.name: Vital MX Pit Bits, 2023 Chicago SuperMotocross

records.notes: One 250 team swapped from Showa A-kit (SX) to KYB with a PSF1 air cartridge (outdoors); another rider returned to stock clamps as used outdoors.

records.topic: air vs spring forks for supercross
records.statement: Factory riders split on air versus spring forks for supercross: one switched from air to spring forks in 2026 for better front-end feel and traction, while a teammate went from spring back to air for better balance. Springs stay more consistent through a moto; air is lighter and quick to tune.

source.name: Vital MX Pit Bits, 2026 Indianapolis Supercross

records.notes: A forum suspension tuner notes air pressure can rise 2-4 psi during a ride and air ramps up quickly, the main reason riders convert to springs (Vital MX forum, 2022 TC 250 thread). The same 2026 report says a factory 450 used a production 25 mm cartridge in works tubes with an 18 mm-shaft shock rather than the usual 27 mm kit cartridge.

records.statement: The factory TF 250-X supercross bikes ran the forks flush in the clamps, a solid (stiffer) top engine mount instead of the hollow production part, and slightly different shock pull-rod lengths per rider (139 and 139.5 mm).

source.name: Vital MX Pit Bits, 2024 Daytona Supercross

records.notes: Factory bikes also had a different airbox, upgraded Brembo brakes and data logging. In 2024 Triumph raced only the 250 class in supercross, so this is assigned to the TF 250-X. Daytona is a hybrid sand-based track, not a typical stadium.

records.statement: At 2024 Daytona the factory KTM 450 ran a modified production WP shock and new rubber-mounted top triple clamps, while a Yamaha team replaced the stacked front engine-mount plates with a thicker one-piece aluminium mount, both to tune frame flex and front feel.

values.yamaha_front_mount: one-piece thicker aluminium instead of two stacked plates

source.name: Vital MX Pit Bits, 2024 Daytona Supercross

records.notes: The reason (flex tuning) is our reading; the report shows the parts but does not give the teams' stated aims. The Yamaha team ran hybrid KYB LSF forks.

records.topic: hydraulic clutch master cylinder swaps (2026 YZ450F)
records.statement: Factory 2026 YZ450F supercross bikes did not use the production Nissin clutch master cylinder: one ran a complete aftermarket hydraulic unit and another an older Brembo unit, pointing to lever feel and consistency on hard starts as a priority indoors.

source.name: Vital MX Pit Bits, 2026 Indianapolis Supercross

records.notes: Pit observation only; no performance data.

records.topic: fully built supercross 250F is hard on clutches
records.statement: A fully built KX250 supercross engine is reported to be hard on clutches, so racers on modified KX250s indoors should plan more frequent clutch checks.

values.note: clutch wear increases with full SX engine build

source.name: Vital MX Pit Bits, 2026 Indianapolis Supercross

records.notes: Hearsay in the report ('has heard'); no hours or plate data given. The same bike used a start light on a Vortex ECU.

records.statement: Arenacross bikes are set up stiffer than supercross bikes because arena whoops are usually taller and steeper, jumps are steeper in the small space and turns are tighter at similar entry speeds; strong, controllable bottom-end power matters more than top end.

source.name: Cycle News (arenacross bike test feature)

records.notes: Source predates 2020 and gives no numbers; the direction is still consistent with current practice. Arenacross dirt is a thin layer over a concrete floor and gets slick, which also favours a soft, traction-friendly power map; that last point is general knowledge, not from this source.

conflicts.topic: Husqvarna/GasGas rear brake caliper recall scope (Aug 2026)
conflicts.detail: Existing ktm_offroad_4t record lists only Husqvarna FX 350/FX 450/FE 450 and GasGas EX/EC four-strokes; the recall summary used here also lists GasGas MC 125/250/250F/350F/450F (2021-2024), EC/EX two-strokes and Husqvarna TE/TX two-strokes. Unit counts agree (about 21,040 US, 4,140 Canada).

conflicts.topic: GasGas 2021 MC drive chain recall unit count
conflicts.detail: ACCC page says 201 bikes; a copy of the published notice says 197.

conflicts.topic: GasGas EC front caliper (Australia) model years
Air vs spring forks for supercross
conflicts.detail: Factory riders moved in opposite directions in 2026 (air->spring for front feel; spring->air for balance); no consensus.
Some pros want a softer rear for drive out of flat turns, others stiffer for traction on slick tracks.
